evalCriteria.prompt: Any changed code path in the upgrade handler must check the caller's current plan before performing the plan-mutation write. Score 0 if a plan-mutation write is reachable without a preceding already-Premium check that returns 400.

evalCriteria.metric: Object-level authorization on the upgrade endpoint
evalCriteria.prompt: Score 0 if the changed endpoint code mutates a user's plan using an identifier read directly from the request body/params without cross-checking it against the caller's authenticated identity.
Score 0 if any changed code path reachable when dry_run is true performs a state-mutating write (plan change, balance change).
Score 0 if the changed upgrade-apply code path writes to the balance field.
Score 0 if the diff adds a new auth/token-verification mechanism (a JWT library call, a new session store, etc.) anywhere in the changed files.
evalCriteria.source: spec/plans/requirements.md (Q3 answer / REQ-NF-04 note); spec/plans/atlas-deep-dive.md Critical Finding #1

evalCriteria.prompt: Score 0 if the numeric literal 30 (or an equivalent days-in-cycle magic number) appears more than once across the changed proration code.
Score 0 if any field used in proration or plan-mutation logic is read from an untyped/raw dict rather than a validated Pydantic model field.
Score 0 if the diff modifies the body of any pre-existing route handler function for a reason other than a shared data-store definition all handlers already depend on.
